sector_model: Exchange and clearing house: volume and rate per contract driven revenue, operating margin, interest on performance bonds net of distributions, clearing default exposure, dividends including annual variable. Not a bank or generic industrial.
thesis: CME Group (Nasdaq: CME), largest US derivatives exchange and clearing house. Q3 2026 (10-Q 0001156375-26-000068 filed 2026-10-23): revenue 1,737.3M vs 1,537.6M (+13.0%), operating income 1,141.4M (65.7% margin), net income 1,036.9M, diluted EPS 2.89 vs 2.49. 9M revenue 5,323.6M (+9.3%), NI 3,233.0M (+11.9%), EPS 8.96 vs 7.92. FY2025 (10-K): revenue 6,520.6M, NI 4,072.2M, OCF 4,277.1M, PP&E capex 83.5M. TTM (FY2025 + 9M26 - 9M25): revenue 6,972.3M, NI 4,415.9M, OCF 4,426.8M, capex 93.7M (PP&E only; capitalized software not separated, so FCF about 4,333M is an upper bound). Shares 357.93M Class A (cover 2026-10-14) so market cap 113.8B at 317.97: TTM P/E 25.8x, FCF yield about 3.8%. Debt 3,425M carrying (par 3,450M), cash 2,198.5M (down from 4,416.9M at year end), equity 26.56B. Capital return: 9M dividends 3,637.7M (10.05 per share declared, includes annual variable) versus 9M FCF about 3,232M; buybacks 1.8B in 9M at average 272.89 (Q3 average 255.81, so the stock is now about 24% above Q3 average), 1.0B authorization left. Interest earned on performance bonds and guaranty fund 4,151.5M in 9M less distributions 3,783.9M, so net about 368M. Market view: a toll-booth with 63% net margin and near zero capex. What the price assumes: continued double digit volume growth in a volatile-rate year; at 25.8x it is not cheap versus ICE (24x GAAP TTM, run 54) and NDAQ (28.9x). Evidence for: record revenue, operating margin 65.7%, low debt, cash conversion above 98% of NI. Gap closing needs: durable volume growth and a valuation below peers, neither shown.
counterthesis: Revenue is tied to market volatility and rates; 2026 growth may be a high-activity peak and the shares are about 24% above the Q3 buyback price. Dividends (3.6% yield, annual variable) already exceed free cash flow in 9M, and cash fell 2.2B in nine months, so payout depends on drawing cash. FCF uses PP&E capex only, so true FCF may be lower. Competition from ICE, Cboe, Eurex and new venues, a Treasury clearing mandate shift, CFTC rule changes, and a clearing default (guaranty fund) are tail risks; the Class B shareholder case is on appeal. Impairments of 28.9M on private investments are small. The 10-Q MD&A, 10-K risk factors and the 2026 Q3 earnings release (non-GAAP) were not read; no peer or own-history multiples beyond aggregator data (CME trailing PE 26.1, forward 24.6, EV/EBITDA 23.3 on stockanalysis) were compared.
invalidation: Thesis fails if average daily volume falls materially from 2026 levels, interest-income net of distributions declines, free cash flow stops covering the regular dividend, or a competitor or regulator takes share of core rate and equity-index contracts.
